messages:
alex_support: customer reported a tool call failing with 400 when they paste a Windows path into the tool args. says it started after switching from mac to windows. error: "Invalid tool args: unexpected control character at position 28"

julie_cs: can you paste the exact payload they sent? any repro curl would be super helpful.

alex_support: here's what they pasted — they copied from Notepad and sent via our web console. i sanitized usernames.

alex_support: ```json
{
  "tool": "file_reader",
  "args": "{\"path\": \"C:\\Users\\alice\\notes.txt\",}"
}
```

alex_support: note the trailing comma inside the inner JSON string and the plain backslashes from Windows. console shows 400 but stacktrace points to our args parser choking on control char (CR).

ingrid_repro: repro'd locally — if you paste that exact payload it fails with same message. looks like the client is sending a raw string that contains unescaped CRLF bytes (\r\n) inside the JSON value, not the escaped sequence \\r\\n.

eng_sam: thanks — two likely issues here: 1) trailing comma inside the inner JSON string (invalid JSON once parsed), 2) unescaped control chars (CR) breaking our strict JSON decoder. either one can trigger the parser error.

eng_sam: quick repro curl that fails (copied from console request):

eng_sam: ```bash
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.com/v1/toolcall \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"tool":"file_reader","args":"{\"path\": \"C:\\Users\\alice\\notes.txt\",}"}'
```

eng_sam: the inner JSON is sent as a raw string and has a trailing comma plus raw backslashes. our server attempts to json.loads(args) and fails because the string contains a CR (from the user's Notepad paste) and a trailing comma.

julie_cs: customer says they pasted straight from explorer address bar. they don't understand escaping. they expect paths to just work.

eng_sam: workaround for them: build args as a proper JSON object on the client and then JSON.stringify it (or use the SDK's tool call helper) so backslashes are escaped and no trailing comma is included. example for JS client:

eng_sam: ```js
const argsObj = { path: "C:\\Users\\alice\\notes.txt" };
await client.toolCall({ tool: 'file_reader', args: JSON.stringify(argsObj) });
```

eng_sam: server-side fix candidates: 1) sanitize incoming tool args to reject/normalize raw control chars with clearer error message, 2) detect common Windows path patterns and suggest escaping in the error payload, 3) try lenient parse fallback (risky). leaning toward (1) + better error messaging.

alex_support: can we add an immediate short-term improvement to the error so support can forward a helpful message? e.g., "tool args appear to include unescaped control characters or trailing commas. please ensure args are valid JSON; on Windows escape backslashes (\\) or use JSON.stringify from your client."

eng_sam: yes — i'll open an eng-runtime ticket and add a clear error code (TOOLARGS_INVALID_ESCAPING) and a pointer to a KB article with example fixes.

dev-bot: created issue RINF-4357 in eng-runtime: "Improve error for unescaped control chars / trailing commas in tool args" assigned to @eng_sam.

julie_cs: pinging customer with workaround + we can link the issue for follow-up. thanks all :thumbsup:
